evidence_boundary: Phase 4 proves deterministic bounded lexical retrieval over immutable FetchedDocument values: Unicode lexical tokenization, overlapping bounded text chunking with stable source provenance and chunk IDs, in-memory BM25 scoring, positive-match filtering, deterministic tie ordering, hard request caps, frozen-plan conformance, and Python 3.11-3.14 execution across Ubuntu, Windows, and macOS. It does not prove semantic embeddings, vector retrieval, hybrid fusion, reranking, persistent indexes, real-world relevance quality, REST, MCP, or production deployment.

requirements.requirement: FetchedDocument text is split into deterministic bounded overlapping TextChunk values with immutable source URL, chunk index, stable chunk ID, text, and token count.
Lexical retrieval applies deterministic in-memory BM25 scoring, returns only positive-score hits up to the requested limit, and resolves equal scores with stable provenance ordering.
Lexical retrieval rejects empty/oversized queries and out-of-policy document, chunk, overlap, per-document chunk, and result limits before unbounded retrieval work.
The implemented retrieve-to-chunk/rank/tokenize call graph conforms to the frozen Phase 4 BEFORE plan.
